headline: Chris Evans digitally removed from Avengers: Doomsday trailer
post:
Hey everyone! It turns out Marvel Studios pulled some sneaky editing tricks for the "Avengers: Doomsday" marketing. According to The Direct, the studio digitally removed Chris Evans' Steve Rogers from a wide shot in the original trailer to protect his big entrance at the very end. 

A brand new teaser posted in October 2026 shows Steve standing right next to Ebon Moss-Bachrach's Ben Grimm, aka The Thing, during the Watchtower scene where Chris Hemsworth's Thor gathers the heroes to face Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor Von Doom. In the initial wide shot, however, Steve was missing entirely! 🎬

This kind of digital manipulation shouldn't surprise us too much anymore. We saw similar editing back when Andrew Garfield and Tobey Maguire were removed from "Spider-Man: No Way Home" footage. What do you think about these sneaky trailer edits? 

#AvengersDoomsday #ChrisEvans #MarvelStudios
original_title: Marvel Studios Secretly Removed Chris Evans From An Avengers: Doomsday Trailer Scene

headline: LEGO Announces New Batman Arkham Batmobile
post:
Hey everyone, we have some fun news for your collection shelves! According to Screen Rant, a brand-new LEGO set inspired by Rocksteady Games' beloved series is officially on the way.

The upcoming release is set number 67009 and features the iconic Batmobile from Batman: Arkham Knight. Scheduled to launch on January 1, 2027, the 317-piece build will cost $29.99 and includes a Batman minifigure based on his design from the game. 🦇

LEGO revealed the addition on its official website, noting that the set is intended for ages nine and up. It even comes with a bonus digital reward that lets you add a golden effect to characters and vehicles in LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight by scanning a QR code inside the box.

Will you be adding this detailed Batmobile build to your display?

#BatmanArkham #LEGO #Batmobile
original_title: New Batman: Arkham Release Officially Confirmed For 2027
